original_text: report/convergence.py is the project's convergence gate: it reads a finished run's summary.json plus each replicate's diagnostics.json, writes convergence.json and convergence.csv into the run directory, and exits non-zero if the run should not be quoted. Replicate pairwise overlap, median span, per-epoch ESS and surviving distinct prior draws are reported with no pass/fail because the project states no threshold for them.

original_text: Mach, heading/track and altitude are NOT fixed over a flight in this engine: three independent exponential clocks (next_turn, next_acceleration, next_climb) share the time constant tau and are redrawn from the Gibbs update after every resampling; at an acceleration the Mach target is redrawn uniformly from the whole mach_range, at a climb altitude is redrawn in 1,000 ft steps, at a turn the control angle changes by uniform +/-180 deg. Multi-manoeuvre paths are generated freely; the posterior's preference for few manoeuvres is inference, not a constraint (Davey p. 103: a sequence of random turns rarely cancels when a straight path would fit).

original_text: Three prior-support limits block piloted end-of-flight scenarios (results/shoulder-comparison.md sec. 7-8). (1) The altitude floor is 25,000 ft, so a descent begun before 00:11 cannot be sampled at all. (2) Vertical rate is absent from the BFO model — Davey states this explicitly at p. 63 — so even with the floor opened a descending particle is scored with a level-flight BFO; this must land before or with any altitude change. (3) The three manoeuvre clocks are independent (Davey p. 60: simultaneity 'not precluded but not favoured') and turns are undirected uniform +/-180 deg, so coordinated slow-turn-descend sequences are under-weighted by prior SHAPE, which no ensemble size fixes. Agreed approach: a planned-descent stratum with its own particle budget floored at 500 ft (the lowest ERA5 grid node) rather than one wider uniform prior; one manoeuvre clock plus a categorical over manoeuvre type, which nests Davey exactly at rate 3/tau with equal singleton weights so make regress keeps a …

Davey's reference [31] is NOAA's IGRF grid calculator (ngdc.noaa.gov/geomag-web/#igrfgrid), not the World Magnetic Model, and in 2014 it served IGRF-11 (last main-field epoch 2010.0, so March 2014 was extrapolated 4.19 years on predicted SV; IGRF-12 was agreed only Dec 2014). Difference at FL350 on 2014-03-08, IGRF-11 minus IGRF-14: mean -0.108 deg, max 0.154 deg over the box; mean -0.088 deg in the 30-37S corridor, vs a control-angle OU sd of 0.0826 deg. original_text: Mode handling in the base estimate: the PRIOR over the five autopilot modes is EQUAL (1:1:1:1:1) - it is the particle ALLOCATION that is unequal (particles_per_mode = [1M, 0.5M, 2.5M, 0.5M, 2.5M]), tuned to expected posterior mass. Measured per mode: P(mode|D) = TH 0.0593, MH 0.0032, TT 0.5427, MT 0.0146, LNAV 0.3802; P(shoulder|mode) = 0.263, 0.522, 0.010, 0.547, 0.016; share of shoulder mass = 42.4%, 4.6%, 14.9%, 21.7%, 16.4%; distinct roots in the 34.5-36.5S band = 3710, 1415, 5304, 1127, 5243. So the two magnetic modes get 7.1% of the particle budget each while carrying ~52-55% conditional shoulder probability - the allocation starves the modes that make the shoulder. Inverting the allocation for shoulder-focused runs would cut its Monte Carlo error without changing the answer in expectation.

The mechanism is mode reweighting toward MH and MT, which carry the shoulder. Log evidence is NOT comparable across these runs because changing σ changes the likelihood's normalising constant.

original_text: MECHANISM at 19:41, and a correction to the naive GDOP analogy: weak conditioning alone gives a FLAT likelihood, which would raise ESS rather than collapse it. Near closest approach the map from along-track position to range is quadratic, rho(s) ~ rho_min + s^2/2R - a fold. rho_min is set by the path's CROSS-track offset and cross-track sensitivity is undiminished (6.95 us/NM), so the likelihood is flat in one direction and has a hard edge in the other: a particle whose closest approach exceeds the observed range is excluded whatever its timing. Importance weights degenerate at that boundary, not at a peak. Consistent with the recorded 19:41 BTO log factors spanning -1704 to -4.34, which is a cliff rather than a peak.

[sampler] temper_epochs / temper_stages: a named epoch's log-likelihood increment is paid out as L^beta over equal stages, with a resample and the invariant rejuvenation kernel between stages, accepted against the TEMPERED ratio. original_text: THE UNIFYING DIAGNOSIS, now complete across five interventions. Look-ahead, resample-move rejuvenation and Davey's branching all act on WHICH PARTICLES GET COPIED; resampling redistributes a population and cannot narrow the spread of incremental weights the leg's own manoeuvre draws generate, which is what the 19:41 ESS measures - so all three leave it unchanged at matched cost. The arc-bridge acted on the proposal and failed because its dead-reckoned forecast is wrong for the 83% of particles that manoeuvre during the leg. Tempering works because it is the only one needing no forecast: its guide is the likelihood itself, the one exactly computable thing. This is a result about the problem, not just the sampler, and belongs in the paper.

original_text: INTERPRETIVE DECISION on Davey's pruning threshold eta, needed because the book leaves it underdetermined: it states eta as an absolute threshold on a weight whose scale it never fixes, and read literally against unnormalised Gaussian densities a perfectly-fitting path still falls through an e^-25 floor after a few epochs from the repeated division by n-bar alone. The engine therefore rescales the population each epoch so its best member sits at weight one, banking the shift exactly into the evidence, making eta read as 'this many nats behind the best surviving path'. That is the only reading on which Davey's tabulated n-bar (3-10) and eta (e^-25 or e^-30) are mutually consistent.

original_text: THE NORTHERN ISLAND IS A LOITERING POPULATION, not a tail of the main one. Weighted over 311,050 final-state particles in the 26-31S band against 13.2M south of 34.5S: autopilot mode INVERTS (island magnetic track 47% / true heading 31%, the two modes that curve with declination; main body true track 57% / LNAV 31%); island turns 2.38 vs 1.13, speed changes 2.92 vs 1.47, altitude changes 2.80 vs 1.68, tau 3.24 h vs 5.05 h, Mach 0.780 vs 0.796, longitude at 00:19 99.3E vs 88.1E. The paths fly south like everything else then double back and zig-zag between roughly 20 and 31S, satisfying the arcs by NOT covering ground. Reaching that region takes several manoeuvres and the manoeuvre prior charges for each, which is why it carries only half a percent. This is a genuine feature of Davey's model - nothing in the published formulation forbids a loitering path and the uniform +/-180 degree turn prior makes it reachable.

original_text: satcom::FinalBfoModel is FULLY IMPLEMENTED with tests and has exactly three forms, selected by which config keys are present: NoOffset (no keys - the cruise model, measurement noise only); Inflated { sd_hz } (the cruise model with sd_hz replacing the tabulated noise s.d.); and StartupOffset { second_hz: [f64;2], first_minus_second_hz: [f64;2], points: [usize;2] } - a start-up offset added to each measured BFO where the second burst's offset is uniform on second_hz and the first is larger by a uniform first_minus_second_hz (one shared start-up event), integrated by Gauss-Legendre quadrature with `points` nodes per range. satcom::FinalBfo::new(&model) builds the quadrature nodes. original_text:
How the handoff_epochs snapshot is implemented (filter.rs, handoff.rs, config.rs):
- Each mode takes its draw at the end of the epoch's loop iteration, after update, tempering and resampling, using stream(5100+k,0).
- Mode probabilities come from each mode's log_evidence to that epoch.
- Stratified selection uses rng stream u64::MAX-2-e.
- Output goes to <seed dir>/handoff-<epoch>/.
- final_row = handoff::NO_FINAL_ROW (i64::MAX as usize; NaN in handoff.npy), because the filter resamples afterwards.
- It is refused with sampler.branching, because branching weights are unnormalised between epochs.
The auxiliary BTO look-ahead is folded in and divided out within the same iteration, so it does not contaminate a snapshot.

original_text: Deterministic path-screen convention for the waypoint work: fly at constant ground speed over a grid with three altitudes (31k/35k/39k ft) and a post-transition track/speed grid. Score BTO as Gaussian with per-row sd. Score BFO with the bias marginalised analytically on its N(150, 25²) Hz prior and 7 Hz noise, which equals the filter's Kalman marginal at zero drift. Compare every path with the best free single-turn path. CAVEAT: the first screen started from the filter's own 18:21:49 position (about 6.81N 96.57E, bearing 295.6°), which inherits the suspect 295.66° prior track and sits 12–26 NM north of N571. The best free turn at 18:39:49 near 7.9N 94.25E (close to SAMAK) and the fixed-start rankings should be re-run from 10 NM past MEKAR at 18:22:12. The coverage maps describe the runs as they stand.

original_text:
The G-turn piloted turn model is in engine/hypotheses/end-of-flight/manoeuvre.rs, with overlay full/piloted-turns.toml for run I.
- Before the terminal window: Davey turns (Poisson, tau log-uniform on the core's Jeffreys prior 0.1–10 h, angle uniform).
- Terminal window opens when height/descent rate ≤ 1500 s, or at the ditching approach.
- In the window, all optional and not exclusive: random uniform turns at a log-uniform rate of 1/h to 1 per 2 min (ln-rate range −4.094 to −0.693); a sweep of 1–3 orbits, proposal 0.5, starting 0–900 s into the window; and for ditching attempts a circuit, proposal 0.5: downwind 60–300 s, base 30–120 s, final into wind or across wind (swell proxy) 0.5/0.5.
- Bank 10–30 deg. A pending sweep is flown before the circuit.
- Latents: davey_tau_h, turns_*_begun, terminal_window_unix_s, sweep/circuit eligible/drawn/begun, circuit_final_kind, heading_change_deg.

original_text:
Engine determinism: each draw comes from stream(seed, stratum, step, particle), a ChaCha8Rng whose stream id is ((stratum<<16 | step)<<32) | particle. Reductions are fixed-order chunked sums. Reserved step tags:
- 0: prior
- 2000+k: resample
- 3000: route samples
- 4000+k: residual snapshot
- 5000/5100/5150: hand-off
- 6000+k: tempering
- 8000–8200: branching
- 9100/9200: moves
- 9500–9800: rejuvenation
- u64::MAX…: route draw and stop hand-off

Adding an epoch renumbers every later step, so runs with different observation sets (e.g. run J with m1825r600 vs run I) can only be compared statistically. Off-by-default keys must be proven byte-identical with gates B/C each time.

original_text: ELT non-detection (evidence register B2) is implemented as a labelled sensitivity, smoke/elt_sensitivity.py, with P(no alert) = delta + (1-delta)(1-p_class). Classes: ditching-like (|FPA| ≤ 10° and v ≤ 100 m/s), high-energy (v > 212 m/s or |FPA| ≥ 30°), and intermediate.
